issues.description: Field mismatch for Animal.name: the problem statement's textual instructions (problem_statement.md lines 84-86) explicitly require using a StringBuilder for the Animal.name attribute, but the UML in the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 26-29) shows the attribute typed as String, and the reference implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java line 4) declares the field as a String (private String name;). This three-way inconsistency (textual requirement vs UML vs solution) can confuse students about the expected field type and the correct getter/setter signatures to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the requirement and the reference implementation consistent. Option A: Update the problem statement to remove or change the StringBuilder instruction so it specifies name: String (matching the UML and reference solution). Option B: Change the reference implementation (and any template skeleton) to store the name as a StringBuilder and update the getter/setter API and all call sites (e.g., use getName().toString() where a String is needed, or provide helper methods) so the code matches the textual instruction. Also update the UML to match whichever type is chosen (String or StringBuilder) so the problem statement is internally consistent.
